rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 133 (maintainer, Meta/Artifact-locations): 'team-worthy rules flagged for separate PR against the team's rules home (`CLAUDE.md` at root, `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, or `AGENTS.md`, whichever the repo uses). See `reference/claude-code-for-engineers.md § 1`.' AGENTS.md is not one of the six auto-load surfaces this rule enumerates, and this repo's own canonical reference states the fact plainly: `ae101--reference--claude-code-for-engineers.md §8`, '`AGENTS.md`: Claude Code does not read it' without an explicit `@AGENTS.md` import from a CLAUDE.md. Listing AGENTS.md alongside `CLAUDE.md`/`.claude/CLAUDE.md` as an equally-valid 'team's rules home' — without the import caveat — is the §4 'vocabulary is a claim' failure mode this compendium names directly: it implies Claude Code reads a PR filed there the same way it reads the other two. Compounding: the pointer names `§ 1` ('The memory hierarchy: where your rules actually live'), which lists only the four native CLAUDE.md-family layers and never mentions AGENTS.md at all — the AGENTS.md nuance lives at §8, not §1, so a trainer following the pointer to check the claim won't find it addressed. Harm: narrow (trainer-only Meta note, not core student teaching; a student whose repo already has an @import wired suffers nothing) but real — a trainer advising 'PR your rule to AGENTS.md' on a repo without the import wires a rule that Claude Code silently never reads, the exact silent-failure shape this compendium repeatedly flags (§40, §49).
